q.s: Shravasti and Saket were the capitals of which of the following Mahajanapadas?
q.x: Koshala had two capitals, Shravasti and Saket (Ayodhya). Vatsa's capital was Kaushambi.

q.s: Kushinara, where the Buddha attained Mahaparinirvana, was a capital of which Mahajanapada?
q.x: The Mallas ruled from Kushinara and Pava (Pawa); the Buddha died at Kushinara.

q.s: Vaishali was the capital of which of the following Mahajanapadas?
q.x: Vaishali was the seat of the Vajji (Vriji) confederacy, which covered the Vaishali-Muzaffarpur-Darbhanga region.

q.s: Which of the following was NOT among the sixteen Mahajanapadas?
q.x: Kalinga does not appear in the Anguttara Nikaya list of sixteen Mahajanapadas; Anga, Chedi and Vajji do.

q.s: Kaushambi on the Yamuna was the capital of which of the following Mahajanapadas?
q.x: Kaushambi was the capital of Vatsa; Mathura was the capital of Surasena.

q.s: Mahishmati was the southern capital of which Mahajanapada, whose northern capital was Ujjayini?
q.x: Avanti had Ujjayini as its northern and Mahishmati as its southern capital.

q.s: Kashi, ruled by the Brahmadatta dynasty, was annexed by which of the following Mahajanapadas?
q.x: Kashi was absorbed by Koshala; the Pradyotas ruled Avanti, not Kashi.

q.s: Which of the following Mahajanapadas did NOT lie in present-day Bihar?
q.x: Kashi (Varanasi) lay in present Uttar Pradesh; Anga, Magadha and Vajji lay in Bihar.

q.s: Which of the following statements about the gana-sanghas is correct?
o: The assembly hall of a gana-sangha was called the Santhagara.
A gana-sangha was ruled by a single hereditary king.
Gana-sanghas had no assemblies of clan heads.
Kamboja remained a monarchy throughout ancient times.
q.x: Gana-sanghas were ruled by assemblies of clan heads meeting in the Santhagara; Kamboja, a monarchy in the 6th century BCE, is a sangha in the Arthashastra.

q.s: Which was the most powerful clan of the eight-clan Vajji confederacy?
q.x: The Lichchhavis of Vaishali led the Vajji confederacy; the Shakyas were a separate republic at Kapilavastu.

q.s: Chetaka, the Lichchhavi chief of the Vajji confederacy, was the maternal uncle of:
q.x: Chetaka's sister Trishala was the mother of Mahavira.

q.s: The Ashtadhyayi, which mentions twenty-two janapadas, was written by:
q.x: Panini, born at Pushkalavati in Gandhara, wrote the Ashtadhyayi in eight chapters.

q.s: According to Buddhist tradition, which Haryanka king killed his father Bimbisara to seize the throne?
q.x: Buddhist texts record a patricide chain: Ajatashatru killed Bimbisara, and Udayin in turn is said to have killed Ajatashatru.

q.s: Who among the following is regarded as the real founder of the Magadhan empire?
q.x: Bimbisara of the Haryanka dynasty expanded Magadha through conquest (Anga) and marriage alliances.

q.s: Bimbisara of Magadha annexed which neighbouring kingdom by defeating its king Brahmadatta?
q.x: Bimbisara defeated Brahmadatta of Anga and placed Kunika (Ajatashatru) as viceroy at Champa.

q.s: Ajatashatru of Magadha used his minister Vassakara to sow dissension among the chiefs of:
q.x: Vassakara split the Lichchhavi chiefs, helping Ajatashatru annex the Vajji confederacy.

q.s: By what name is Ajatashatru of Magadha known in Jain texts?
q.x: Jain texts call Ajatashatru Kunika; Seniya (Shrenika) is the Jain name of his father Bimbisara.

q.s: Which Magadhan ruler shifted the capital from Rajagriha to Pataliputra?
q.x: Udayin moved the capital to Pataliputra; Ajatashatru had earlier fortified Pataligrama.

q.s: Which Magadhan ruler temporarily moved the capital to Vaishali?
q.x: Shishunaga moved the capital to Vaishali; his son Kalashoka moved it back to Pataliputra.

q.s: Which dynasty ruled Magadha immediately before the Nandas?
q.x: The order was Haryanka, Shishunaga and then Nanda; the Mauryas followed the Nandas.

q.s: The Hathigumpha inscription, which refers to a canal dug by a Nanda king, belongs to:
q.x: The Hathigumpha inscription at Udayagiri is Kharavela's; the Junagadh inscription is Rudradaman I's.

q.s: The Second Buddhist Council was held at Vaishali during the reign of:
q.x: Kalashoka of the Shishunaga dynasty held the Second Council at Vaishali; the First was at Rajagriha under Ajatashatru.

q.s: Which Shishunaga ruler destroyed the power of Avanti and annexed it to Magadha?
q.x: Shishunaga ended the power of the Pradyotas of Avanti.

q.s: Which of the following titles of Mahapadma Nanda means 'destroyer of all Kshatriyas'?
q.x: Sarvakshatrantaka means destroyer of all Kshatriyas; Ekarat means sole sovereign.

q.s: According to the Puranas, the earliest dynasty of Magadha was the:
q.x: The Puranas name the Brihadratha line, to which Jarasandha belonged, as Magadha's first dynasty; it ruled from Girivraja.

q.s: Which of the following was NOT a factor in the rise of Magadha?
o: Control of the Arabian Sea ports
q.x: Magadha rose on iron, fertile soil and river routes; it had no Arabian Sea coast.

q.s: Alexander fought the Battle of the Hydaspes against Porus in the year:
q.x: Alexander crossed the Hindu Kush in 327 BC, fought Porus on the Hydaspes (Jhelum) in 326 BC, left India in 325 BC and died at Babylon in 323 BC.

q.s: The Battle of the Hydaspes between Alexander and Porus was fought on the banks of which river?
q.x: The Hydaspes is the Jhelum; Alexander founded Bucephala and Nicaea there.

q.s: Alexander's army refused to advance further into India on the banks of which river?
q.x: The army mutinied at the Beas (Hyphasis), partly out of fear of the Nanda army; twelve altars were raised there.

q.s: The Nanda king called 'Agrammes' by the Greeks, a contemporary of Alexander, was:
q.x: Dhana Nanda, the last Nanda, was Alexander's contemporary; Bhaddasala commanded his army.

q.s: The kingdom of Porus, who fought Alexander, lay between which two rivers?
q.x: Porus ruled between the Jhelum and the Chenab; Takshashila lay between the Indus and the Jhelum.

q.s: Which Achaemenid ruler made Sindh and the Punjab west of the Indus the twentieth satrapy of his empire?
q.x: Darius I created the Indian (20th) satrapy, which per Herodotus paid 360 talents of gold dust.

q.s: Who among the following was the envoy of Antiochus I to the court of Bindusara?
q.x: Deimachus came to Bindusara; Megasthenes was Seleucus Nicator's envoy to Chandragupta Maurya.

q.s: Which of the following writers did NOT accompany Alexander to India?
q.x: Arrian wrote much later; Nearchus, Onesicritus and Aristobulus left first-hand accounts.

q.s: The last Kanva ruler, Susharman, was overthrown by the Satavahana ruler:
q.x: Simuka, founder of the Satavahana line, ended the Kanva dynasty.

q.s: The last Sunga king Devabhuti was killed by his minister, who founded the Kanva dynasty. He was:
q.x: Vasudeva Kanva killed Devabhuti and founded the Kanva dynasty.

q.s: According to the Puranas, which dynasty defeated the Sungas and the Kanvas?
q.x: The Puranas say the Satavahanas (Andhras) overthrew the Kanvas and the remnant Sungas.

q.s: Which of the following is NOT associated with the Sunga period?
q.x: The Sunga age saw Brahmanical revival, Bhagavatism and stone Buddhist art at Bharhut and Sanchi; the Gandhara school flourished under the Kushanas.

q.s: Agnimitra, the hero of Kalidasa's Malavikagnimitram, was viceroy of the Sungas at:
q.x: Agnimitra, son of Pushyamitra, governed Vidisha.

q.s: Pushyamitra Sunga founded his dynasty by killing which Mauryan king?
q.x: Per the Harshacharita, Pushyamitra, a Brahmin general, killed Brihadratha while showing him the army.

q.s: Which text described foreigners absorbed into Indian society as 'Vratya Kshatriyas'?
q.x: The Manusmriti, compiled around the Sunga period, called them Vratya (degenerate) Kshatriyas.

q.s: The Besnagar Garuda pillar was erected in honour of Vasudeva by Heliodorus, envoy of the Indo-Greek king:
q.x: Heliodorus came from Taxila as envoy of Antialcidas to the Sunga king Bhagabhadra.

q.s: In which language is the inscription on the Besnagar pillar of Heliodorus written?
q.x: It is in Prakrit in the Brahmi script, not Greek.

q.s: The Bharhut stupa, whose inscriptions record gifts by ordinary donors and guilds, is in which present state?
q.x: Bharhut is in Satna district of Madhya Pradesh.

q.s: Which school of sculpture is said to have begun under the Sungas?
q.x: The Mathura school began in the Sunga period; Gandhara is linked to the Kushanas and Amaravati to the Satavahanas.

q.s: Which of the following was the capital of the Kadambas?
q.x: The Kadambas ruled from Vanavasi (Banavasi); Vatapi was the Chalukya capital, Manyakheta the Rashtrakuta capital.

q.s: The Chalukya dynasty of Badami (Vatapi) was founded by:
q.x: Pulakesin I founded the Badami Chalukyas; Pulakesin II was its greatest ruler.

q.s: Indo-Greek coins were mostly made of:
q.x: Most Indo-Greek coins were silver and copper; more than 30 Indo-Greek kings are known mainly from them.

q.s: Who were the first to issue gold coins in India?
q.x: The Indo-Greeks issued the first (rare) gold coins; the Kushanas later issued gold on a large scale.

q.s: Which of the following statements is correct?
o: Heliodorus came as the envoy of Menander to Bhagabhadra.
Daimachos was sent by Antiochus I to the court of Bindusara.
The Besnagar pillar of Heliodorus honours Sankarshana.
The Smritis called the Greeks absorbed into Indian society Shudras.
q.x: Daimachos came to Bindusara. Heliodorus was Antialcidas's envoy, the pillar honours Vasudeva, and the Smritis called the Greeks Vratya Kshatriyas.

q.s: Who was the first Bactrian Greek ruler to cross the Hindu Kush and invade India, around 180 BCE?
q.x: Demetrius led the first Bactrian Greek invasion; Diodotus founded Bactria by revolting against the Seleucids.

q.s: The Kushanas were defeated around 90 AD by which Chinese general?
q.x: The Kushanas marched against Pan Chao after a Han princess was refused to their king, and were defeated.

q.s: The Kushanas belonged to which of the following groups of tribes?
q.x: The Kushanas were one of the five clans of the Yuezhi.

q.s: Which of the following was a capital of Kanishka?
q.x: Kanishka ruled from Purushapura (Peshawar), with Mathura as a second capital.

q.s: Kanishka was the son of which Kushana ruler?
q.x: Vima Kadphises was Kanishka's father; the Rabatak inscription gives the genealogy.

q.s: The Rabatak inscription, which gives the genealogy of Kanishka, is written in which language?
q.x: It is in the Bactrian language in Greek script, found near Surkh Kotal in Afghanistan.

q.s: The Saka era, on which India's national calendar has been based since 1957, began in the year:
q.x: The Saka era began in 78 CE; the Vikrama era began in 57 BCE, 135 years earlier.

q.s: Which of the following statements about the Saka era is correct?
o: It began 135 years before the Vikrama era.
It was founded by Chandragupta II after defeating the Sakas.
It is also called the Salivahana Saka, a legend crediting it to Gautamiputra Satakarni.
It was never used by the Western Kshatrapas.
q.x: The 78 CE era is also called the Salivahana Saka; it is named Saka because the Western Kshatrapas used it, and it began 135 years after the Vikrama era.

q.s: Which Kushana ruler is credited with issuing the first Kushana gold coins?
q.x: Vima Kadphises first issued gold coins, often showing Shiva with a trident and bull; Kujula Kadphises issued copper coins.

q.s: On Kanishka's coins, Shiva appears under the name:
q.x: Kanishka's coins show over thirty deities, including the Buddha (BODDO) and Shiva as Oesho.

q.s: Surkhi, a brick-dust lime mortar, is first found in the Kushana levels at which site?
q.x: Surkhi first appears in Kushana-period levels at Mathura; the Shakas and Kushanas also brought new dress and better cavalry.

q.s: The main medium used by the Gandhara school of art was:
q.x: Gandhara used blue-grey schist and stucco; spotted red sandstone was Mathura's medium and white marble Amaravati's.

q.s: The Gandhara school of art was mainly associated with which form of Buddhism?
q.x: Gandhara art expressed Mahayana, showing the Buddha in human form and Bodhisattvas such as Avalokiteshvara and Maitreya.

q.s: Which of the following is NOT a feature of the Gandhara school of art?
o: Use of grey schist and stucco
q.x: The shaven-headed Buddha belongs to the early Mathura school; the Gandhara Buddha has wavy hair and heavy drapery.

q.s: The Mathura school of art worked mainly in which material?
q.x: Mathura used spotted red sandstone and flourished under the Kushanas, producing Buddhist, Jain and Brahmanical icons.

q.s: Which of the following is NOT a feature of the Mathura school of art?
o: Images of Hindu and Jain deities
q.x: Blue-grey schist was the Gandhara medium; Mathura worked in red sandstone and made Buddhist, Jain and Brahmanical images.

q.s: The Tamil epic Silappadikaram was written by:
q.x: Ilango Adigal, brother of the Chera king Senguttuvan, wrote the Silappadikaram; Sattanar wrote the Manimekalai.

q.s: In the Silappadikaram, Kovalan is executed on the orders of a king of which dynasty?
q.x: The Pandya king at Madurai had Kovalan executed, and Kannagi burnt Madurai in revenge.

q.s: How many couplets does the Tirukkural contain?
q.x: The Tirukkural, called Ulaga Podhumarai, has 1,330 couplets in three books: Aram, Porul and Inbam.

q.s: Which book of the Tirukkural deals with love?
q.x: Aram deals with virtue, Porul with wealth and polity, and Inbam (Kamattuppal) with love.

q.s: Sangam literature, consisting of about 2,400 poems, was composed in which language?
q.x: Sangam literature is in old Tamil and includes poems by women poets.

q.s: In Sangam poetry, 'puram' poems mainly deal with:
q.x: Puram poems deal with war, valour and royal deeds; aham poems deal with love.

q.s: The generally accepted span of the Sangam age is:
q.x: The Sangam age is usually dated c. 300 BCE to 300 CE; 3rd-century BCE Tamil-Brahmi inscriptions support its early limit.

q.s: Which of the following statements about the Sangam age is correct?
o: Sangam literature was composed in Prakrit.
The contemporary Satavahanas used Prakrit in their records.
Tamil-Brahmi inscriptions mark the later limit of the Sangam age.
The Sangam age is dated c. 600-900 CE.
q.x: Sangam literature is in old Tamil while the Satavahanas used Prakrit; Tamil-Brahmi inscriptions support the early limit.

q.s: Arikamedu, an Indo-Roman trading settlement of the Sangam age, lies near:
q.x: Arikamedu is near Puducherry; Keezhadi is on the Vaigai in Sivaganga district.

q.s: The Pugalur inscription records three generations of rulers of which Sangam dynasty?
q.x: The Pugalur (Aranattarmalai) Tamil-Brahmi inscription records three generations of Chera rulers.

q.s: What was the royal emblem of the Cholas in the Sangam age?
q.x: The Cholas had the tiger, the Pandyas the fish and the Cheras the bow.

q.s: Which of the following was NOT a Chola capital or port of the Sangam age?
q.x: Madurai was the Pandya capital; the Cholas ruled from Uraiyur and Puhar (Kaveripattinam).

q.s: Karikala Chola defeated the Cheras, the Pandyas and eleven chieftains in the Battle of:
q.x: Karikala won at Venni; Talaiyalanganam was the Pandya Nedunjeliyan's victory.

q.s: Which Sangam work celebrates Karikala Chola as its hero?
q.x: Karikala is the hero of the Pattinappalai; the Maduraikanchi praises the Pandya Nedunjeliyan.

q.s: The Pattini cult, the worship of Kannagi, was started by which Chera ruler?
q.x: Senguttuvan, the 'Red Chera', brought the stone for the idol from the Himalayas; Gajabahu of Sri Lanka attended the consecration.

q.s: Pliny described which Chera port as the 'first emporium of India'?
q.x: Muziris was the great Chera port where a temple of Augustus is said to have stood.

q.s: In the Sangam age, the minor hill and forest chieftains were known as:
q.x: The Velir were minor chieftains; the seven vallals were famous patron chieftains.

q.s: Who excavated the Indo-Roman trading site of Arikamedu in 1945?
q.x: Mortimer Wheeler excavated Arikamedu in 1945. Muziris has been identified with Pattanam in Kerala.

q.s: Which of the following was NOT a major export from South India to Rome in the Sangam age?
q.x: India exported pepper, muslin, pearls and ivory; Roman gold coins flowed into the Tamil country in payment.

q.s: In Sangam society, the Parayar were known as:
q.x: The Parayar were drummers who worked with animal skins; a rigid varna system had not fully developed.

q.s: Puhar (Kaveripattinam), with its prosperous Yavana quarter, was the chief port of the:
q.x: Puhar was the Chola port on the east coast at the mouth of the Kaveri.

q.s: The Sangam port of Korkai was famous for:
q.x: Korkai, the Pandya port, was famed for pearls; Tondi (Tyndis) was a Chera port.

q.s: Which of the following was NOT a port of the Sangam age?
q.x: Uraiyur was the inland Chola capital; Muziris, Korkai and Puhar were ports.

q.s: Which of the following statements about women in the Sangam age is correct?
o: Women were barred from composing poetry.
Nachchellaiyar and Kakkaipadiniyar were women poets.
Sati was unknown in Sangam society.
Women could not own property under any circumstance.
q.x: Women poets such as Nachchellaiyar, Kakkaipadiniyar and Avvaiyar are known; sati existed mainly among the higher strata.

q.s: The Sangam deity Mayon is identified with:
q.x: Mayon is Vishnu; Murugan's six abodes are the Arupadai Veedu, and Korravai was the war goddess.

q.s: The five-fold tinai division of land in the Sangam age is described in the:
q.x: The tinai scheme is set out in the Tolkappiyam.

q.s: In the Sangam tinai scheme, Murugan was the deity of which landscape?
q.x: Murugan belonged to Kurinji (hills); Mayon to Mullai, Vendan to Marutam and Varunan to Neidal.

q.s: The Kalabhra rule over the Tamil country, often called the 'dark age' of Tamil history, lasted roughly during:
q.x: The Kalabhras ruled c. 3rd-6th century CE, patronised Jainism and Buddhism, and were ended by the Pandya Kadungon and the Pallava Simhavishnu.

q.s: Which of the following rulers founded the Pala dynasty of Bengal?
q.x: Gopala was elected king to end anarchy (Matsya Nyaya) in the mid-8th century, after Mahendravarman I and before Pratihara Bhoja.

q.s: Which of the following dynasties was NOT a party to the Tripartite Struggle for Kannauj?
q.x: The 8th-9th century struggle was among the Palas, Pratiharas and Rashtrakutas; Kannauj symbolised imperial sovereignty.

q.s: The exhaustion of the powers in the struggle for Kannauj opened the way for the rise of:
o: The Rajput states such as the Chandelas and Chauhans
q.x: The weakening of the Palas, Pratiharas and Rashtrakutas let Rajput states such as the Chandelas and Chauhans emerge.

q.s: The Pratihara ruler who defeated the Pala king Dharmapala at Monghyr was:
q.x: Nagabhata II defeated Dharmapala at Monghyr (Mudgagiri) and made Kannauj the Pratihara capital.

q.s: The election of Gopala to end Matsya Nyaya is recorded in which inscription?
q.x: The Khalimpur copper plates of Dharmapala record Gopala's election; the Gwalior prashasti is Mihira Bhoja's.

q.s: Vikramashila Mahavihara, a centre of Vajrayana Buddhism, was founded by:
q.x: Dharmapala founded Vikramashila at Antichak in Bhagalpur district of Bihar.

q.s: The Odantapuri Mahavihara, which served as a model for Tibetan monasteries, was founded by:
q.x: Gopala founded Odantapuri; Dharmapala founded Vikramashila and Ramapala Jagaddala.

q.s: Which of the following mahaviharas was NOT founded by a Pala ruler?
q.x: Nalanda was far older (Gupta period); Odantapuri (Gopala), Vikramashila (Dharmapala) and Jagaddala (Ramapala) were Pala foundations.

q.s: The Nava Nalanda Mahavihara, a Pali research centre, was founded by:
q.x: Bhikshu Jagadish Kashyap founded it; President Rajendra Prasad laid its foundation stone in 1951.

q.s: The Shailendra ruler Balaputradeva obtained five villages for his Nalanda monastery from which Pala king?
q.x: Devapala granted the villages at the request of Balaputradeva of Suvarnadvipa.

q.s: The Sena dynasty of Bengal, which succeeded the Palas, originally came from:
q.x: Samantasena came from Karnataka; Vijayasena founded independent Sena rule by expelling Madanapala.

q.s: Danasagara and Adbhutasagara are works attributed to which Sena king?
q.x: Ballalasena, the scholar king, is credited with these works.

q.s: Valabhi under the Maitrakas was a famous centre of learning for which school of Buddhism?
q.x: Valabhi was a Hinayana centre; Nalanda was the Mahayana centre of Harsha's time.

q.s: Which of the following statements about ancient centres of learning is correct?
o: Valabhi was a Mahayana centre under the Maitrakas.
Taxila was the capital of Gandhara.
q.x: Taxila was the Gandhara capital; Valabhi was Hinayana, Nalanda predates the Palas, and Vikramashila was Dharmapala's.

q.s: Gopala, the founder of the Pala dynasty, replaced which ruling family of eastern Bengal?
q.x: Gopala replaced the Khadgas; his election is recorded in Dharmapala's Khalimpur inscription.

q.s: Pala sculpture was chiefly made of:
q.x: Pala sculpture used black stone (basalt) and bronze; Pala painting survives in palm-leaf Buddhist manuscripts.

q.s: The Rashtrakuta king who defeated the Pratihara ruler Nagabhata II was:
q.x: Govinda III defeated Nagabhata II; Dhruva had defeated Vatsaraja.

q.s: The coins of Pratihara king Mihira Bhoja bear the Vaishnava legend:
q.x: Mihira Bhoja, son of Ramabhadra and grandson of Nagabhata II, issued coins with the legend Adivaraha.

q.s: The Gurjara-Pratihara expansion under Mihira Bhoja in the north was checked by which ruler of Kashmir?
q.x: Sankaravarman of Kashmir checked Mihira Bhoja, who had recovered Kannauj around 836 AD.

q.s: The Arab merchant Sulaiman counted which Rashtrakuta king among the four great kings of the world?
q.x: Sulaiman named Amoghavarsha I; he called the Pratihara kingdom Juzr.

q.s: Muhammad bin Qasim conquered Sindh in 712 CE after defeating and killing:
q.x: Raja Dahir was killed in 712; Arab rule thereafter stayed largely confined to Sindh and Multan.

q.s: The Kailasa temple at Ellora, carved from a single rock, was built by which dynasty?
q.x: The Kailasa (Cave 16) was carved under the Rashtrakuta Krishna I from a basalt cliff, with a Dravida vimana.

q.s: The Kailasa temple at Ellora was carved out of which rock?
q.x: It was cut top-down from a single basalt cliff.

q.s: Which group of caves at Ellora is the latest in date?
q.x: The Buddhist caves (1-12) are earliest, the Hindu caves (13-29) mainly Rashtrakuta, and the Jain caves (30-34) of the 9th-10th century the latest.

q.s: The Ellora caves, locally called Verul Leni, are carved in which hills?
q.x: Ellora is cut in the Charanandri hills near Aurangabad (Chhatrapati Sambhajinagar).

q.s: Which of the following cave temples at Ellora is the latest?
q.x: Of these, the Kailasa (Cave 16) is the latest; the Hindu caves were mainly Rashtrakuta work.

q.s: Amoghavarsha I, under whom Jainism reached its peak in the Rashtrakuta kingdom, was a disciple of:
q.x: Amoghavarsha I was a disciple of Jinasena; the Rashtrakutas also let Arab merchants build mosques in port towns.

q.s: The Arab writers' term 'Balhara' for the Rashtrakuta king comes from the Rashtrakuta title:
q.x: Balhara is the Arabic form of Vallabha (Ballaha-raja).

q.s: The Rashtrakuta age raised which language to a classical literary medium?
q.x: Rashtrakuta patronage (Kavirajamarga of Amoghavarsha's court) raised Kannada; the dynasty fell to the Chalukyas of Kalyani in the late 10th century.

q.s: The cave temples of Badami lie around which lake?
q.x: Badami's four sandstone cave temples surround the Agastya lake; the earliest work was under Mangalesha.

q.s: Which of the following is NOT a centre of Badami Chalukya temple architecture?
q.x: Halebid is a Hoysala centre; Aihole, Badami and Pattadakal are Chalukya sites.

q.s: Which place has been called the 'cradle of Indian temple architecture'?
q.x: Aihole, with the apsidal Durga temple and the flat-roofed Lad Khan temple, is called the cradle of Indian temple architecture.

q.s: Which of the following temples is NOT located at Aihole?
q.x: The Virupaksha temple of Vikramaditya II's queen is at Pattadakal.

q.s: The Virupaksha temple at Pattadakal was built to commemorate the victory of Vikramaditya II over the:
q.x: Queen Lokamahadevi built it to mark Vikramaditya II's victory over the Pallavas.

q.s: Which of the following statements about Pattadakal is correct?
o: It was the coronation site of the Badami Chalukyas.
Its Virupaksha temple was built by the Rashtrakutas.
It lies on the banks of the Godavari.
q.x: Pattadakal on the Malaprabha was the Chalukya coronation site, with Nagara and Dravida temples side by side.

q.s: The Virupaksha temple at Pattadakal is modelled on which Pallava temple?
q.x: It was modelled on the Kailasanatha temple of Kanchi; its architects included Gunda Anivaritachari.

q.s: The Pallava king Mahendravarman I was converted from Jainism to Shaivism by:
q.x: Appar (Tirunavukkarasar) converted Mahendravarman I; rock-cut temples in South India began with him.

q.s: The Sanskrit farce Mattavilasa Prahasana was written by:
q.x: Mahendravarman I wrote it, mocking Kapalikas and Buddhist monks; the Kiratarjuniya is Bharavi's.

q.s: Which of the following titles did NOT belong to the Pallava king Mahendravarman I?
q.x: Vatapikonda was the title of Narasimhavarman I after he took Vatapi.

q.s: The Kudumiamalai inscription of the Pallava period, credited to Mahendravarman I, is famous for:
q.x: The Kudumiamalai inscription is a music inscription; the Mandagapattu inscription records a temple made without brick, timber, metal or mortar.

q.s: What was the capital of the Pallavas?
q.x: Kanchipuram was the Pallava capital; Mamallapuram was their port.

q.s: The Pallavas were originally feudatories of which dynasty?
q.x: The Pallavas began as Satavahana feudatories; the Badami Chalukyas were their rivals.

q.s: Which Pallava ruler of Kanchi faced the southern invasion of Samudragupta?
q.x: The Allahabad pillar inscription names Vishnugopa of Kanchi among the kings defeated by Samudragupta.

q.s: Which Pallava king bore the title Pallavamalla and was a contemporary of Tirumangai Alvar?
q.x: Nandivarman II Pallavamalla was placed on the throne as a boy of twelve by the ministers and nobles.

q.s: Mahabalipuram is also called Mamallapuram after the title 'Mamalla' of:
q.x: Narasimhavarman I bore the titles Mamalla and Vatapikonda; Gunabhara and Vichitrachitta were Mahendravarman I's titles.

q.s: The Pallava general who sacked Vatapi under Narasimhavarman I was:
q.x: Paranjoti sacked Vatapi after Narasimhavarman I killed Pulakesin II at Manimangala in 642 CE.

q.s: Which Pallava king defeated and killed the Chalukya Pulakesin II in 642 CE?
q.x: Narasimhavarman I earned the title Vatapikonda after this victory.

q.s: Which is the largest of the Pancha Rathas at Mahabalipuram?
q.x: The Dharmaraja ratha is the largest; the Draupadi ratha is the smallest, a hut-shaped cell.

q.s: Which of the Pancha Rathas at Mahabalipuram has an apsidal plan?
q.x: The Nakula-Sahadeva ratha is apsidal; each ratha is carved from a single granite rock.

q.s: The Shore Temple at Mahabalipuram was built by:
q.x: Rajasimha built the Shore Temple, the sole survivor of the 'Seven Pagodas'; it has two Shiva shrines and one Vishnu shrine.

q.s: Which of the following statements about the Shore Temple at Mahabalipuram is correct?
o: It has two Shiva shrines and one Vishnu shrine.
It was built by Narasimhavarman I.
It is a monolithic rock-cut ratha.
q.x: The Shore Temple is a structural temple of Rajasimha (Narasimhavarman II) at Mahabalipuram with two Shiva shrines and one Vishnu shrine.

q.s: The Kailasanatha temple at Kanchi was built by the Pallava king:
q.x: Rajasimha built it and his son Mahendravarman III completed it; it bears a Kannada inscription of Vikramaditya II.

q.s: The Mandagapattu inscription, recording a temple to Brahma, Vishnu and Shiva, was issued by:
q.x: Mahendravarman I's Mandagapattu inscription says the shrine was made without brick, timber, metal or mortar.

q.s: The Sittannavasal cave paintings in Pudukkottai district belong to which religion?
q.x: Sittannavasal is a Jain cave with lotus-pond murals, renovated by the Pandyas in the 9th century.

q.s: Which of the following was a famous merchant guild of the Chola age?
q.x: The Ayyavole (Five Hundred) and the Manigramam were major merchant guilds that traded overseas and kept their own militias.

q.s: Rajaraja I granted the village of Anaimangalam to the Chudamani Vihara located at:
q.x: The Chudamani Vihara was at Nagapattinam; temple income came from guild donations as well as royal grants.

q.s: The Chudamani Vihara at Nagapattinam was built by a king of which kingdom?
q.x: The Srivijaya king Sri Mara Vijayottunga Varman built it; relations with Srivijaya turned hostile under Rajendra I.

q.s: Which of the following statements about the Chudamani Vihara is correct?
o: It was built by Rajendra I.
Rajaraja I granted the village of Anaimangalam to it.
q.x: Rajaraja I granted Anaimangalam to this Buddhist vihara at Nagapattinam, built by the Srivijaya king.

q.s: Which was the main port of the later (imperial) Cholas?
q.x: Nagapattinam was the chief port of the later Cholas; Puhar was the early Sangam port-capital.

q.s: In the Chola period, 'kasu' referred to a:
q.x: The kasu was a gold coin; nagarams were market centres and erivirappattanas protected mercantile towns.

q.s: Chola bronze images were cast by which technique?
q.x: Chola bronzes used the lost-wax process; queen Sembiyan Mahadevi was a key patron.

q.s: In the Chola Nataraja bronze, the lower right hand held in abhaya mudra signifies:
q.x: Abhaya mudra means 'do not fear', signifying protection.

q.s: The Uttaramerur inscriptions of Parantaka I are important for knowledge of:
o: The kudavolai system of village elections
q.x: The Uttaramerur inscriptions describe the kudavolai (pot-ticket) election to village committees.

q.s: The Dilwara Jain temples are located at:
q.x: The Dilwara temples are at Mount Abu in Rajasthan.

q.s: The Jagannath temple at Puri was founded by:
q.x: Anantavarman Chodaganga of the Eastern Gangas founded it; Narasimhadeva I built the Konark Sun temple.

q.s: The Gangaikondacholapuram temple was built by which Chola ruler?
q.x: Rajendra I built it after his Ganga campaign; it is later than the Brihadeeswara of Rajaraja I.

q.s: The Narthamalai temple, an early Chola stone temple, is associated with which ruler?
q.x: Vijayalaya's Narthamalai (Vijayalaya Cholisvaram) temple is an early Chola temple; the Dravida style peaked under the Cholas.

q.s: Which temple is known as 'Dakshina Meru'?
q.x: The Brihadeeswara temple at Thanjavur, with a granite vimana about 216 ft high, is called Dakshina Meru.

q.s: The 'Musical Steps' are a feature of which Chola temple?
q.x: The Airavatesvara temple at Darasuram has the musical steps and a horse-drawn stone chariot.

q.s: Which of the following temples is NOT part of the UNESCO 'Great Living Chola Temples'?
q.x: Chidambaram is not in the group; Thanjavur was inscribed in 1987 and the other two added in 2004.

q.s: The Chola frescoes in the Brihadeeswara temple show Rajaraja I with his guru:
q.x: The ambulatory frescoes show Shiva as Tripurantaka and Rajaraja I with his guru Karuvur Thevar.

q.s: The Shaiva canon Tirumurai was compiled in the time of Rajaraja I by:
q.x: Nambi Andar Nambi compiled the Tirumurai of the Nayanars; with the Periya Puranam it forms 12 books. The Alvars' hymns form the Nalayira Divya Prabandham.

q.s: The Kalingattupparani, on the Kalinga war of Kulottunga I, was written by:
q.x: Jayamkondar wrote the Kalingattupparani; Pavanandhi wrote the grammar Nannul.

q.s: The Nalayira Divya Prabandham, the 4,000 hymns of the twelve Alvars, was compiled by:
q.x: Nathamuni compiled the Vaishnava Divya Prabandham.

q.s: The Chennakeshava temple at Belur was built in 1117 by the Hoysala king:
q.x: Vishnuvardhana built the Chennakeshava at Belur; the Keshava temple at Somanathapura was built in 1268 under Narasimha III.

q.s: The Hoysaleswara temple at Halebid is dedicated to:
q.x: The Hoysaleswara temple, built c. 1121 by Ketamalla, is a Shiva temple.

q.s: Which of the following is NOT a feature of Hoysala temple architecture?
q.x: Hoysala temples have stellate plans on a jagati and lathe-turned soapstone pillars; towering gopurams are a later Chola-Vijayanagara and Nayaka feature.

q.s: The 'Sacred Ensembles of the Hoysalas' were inscribed on the UNESCO World Heritage List in:
q.x: They were inscribed in 2023; the Ramappa temple (2021) is a separate site.

q.s: Which of the following is NOT a component of the UNESCO 'Sacred Ensembles of the Hoysalas'?
q.x: The Ramappa temple is a separate Kakatiya World Heritage Site (2021).

q.s: The Hoysalas originally began as feudatories of:
q.x: The Hoysalas were feudatories of the Kalyani Chalukyas before becoming independent by the late 12th century.

q.s: What was the original name of the Hoysala king Vishnuvardhana?
q.x: Vishnuvardhana was Bittideva (Bittiga) before his conversion to Vaishnavism by Ramanuja.

q.s: Vishnuvardhana took the title 'Talakadugonda' after capturing Talakad from the:
q.x: He took Talakad from the Cholas.

q.s: According to legend, the Hoysala dynasty originated at Sosevur (Angadi) in which present district of Karnataka?
q.x: The Sala legend is set at Sosevur (Angadi) in Chikkamagaluru district; the Hoysalas were Malnad hill chiefs.

q.s: The Keshava temple at Somanathapura was built during the reign of which Hoysala ruler?
q.x: Somanatha, a general of Narasimha III, built it in 1268. The ruler order was Ereyanga, Vishnuvardhana, Veera Ballala II, Narasimha III.

q.s: The Kannada work Harishchandra Kavya, written in the shatpadi metre, was composed by:
q.x: Raghavanka wrote it; his uncle Harihara popularised the ragale metre.

q.s: The famous 'Darpana Sundari' (lady with a mirror) bracket figure is found at:
q.x: The Darpana Sundari madanika is at the Chennakeshava temple, Belur.

q.s: Which of the following statements about religion under the Hoysalas is correct?
o: Queen Shantala Devi remained a Jain though Vishnuvardhana became a Vaishnava.
After Vishnuvardhana's conversion, the Hoysalas patronised only Vaishnavism.
The Hoysaleswara temple at Halebid is a Vishnu temple.
Jain generals were removed from royal service.
q.x: Patronage stayed plural: Shantala Devi remained Jain, Jain generals like Gangaraja were honoured, and the Hoysaleswara is a Shiva temple.

q.s: Devagiri, the capital of the Yadavas, was renamed Daulatabad by:
q.x: Muhammad bin Tughlaq renamed it Daulatabad and shifted his capital there in 1327.

q.s: The Hemadpanti style of temple architecture, using black basalt laid without mortar, is named after a minister of the:
q.x: Hemadri, Shrikaranadhipa of the Yadavas, gave his name to the Hemadpanti style.

q.s: The Chaturvarga Chintamani, a Sanskrit work on dharma, rituals and vratas, was written by:
q.x: Hemadri, minister of Mahadeva and Ramachandra, wrote the Chaturvarga Chintamani.

q.s: The Chand Minar in the Daulatabad (Devagiri) fort was built by:
q.x: The Chand Minar dates from the 15th-century Bahmani ruler Alauddin; the fort itself was begun by the Yadava Bhillama V.

q.s: Which of the following is NOT traditionally credited to Hemadri, the Yadava minister?
q.x: Mugdhabodha is the grammar of Bopadeva, Hemadri's protege.

q.s: The Mahanubhava sect, whose Lilacharitra is the first Marathi prose work, was founded by:
q.x: Chakradhar Swami founded it in 1267; its literature is mainly in Marathi.

q.s: Which of the following Marathi saints was NOT a contemporary of Dnyaneshwar?
q.x: Tukaram belongs to the 17th century; Namdev, Janabai and Gora Kumbhar were late 13th-14th century Varkari saints.

q.s: What was the capital of Raja Dahir, whom Muhammad bin Qasim defeated in Sindh?
q.x: Dahir ruled from Alor; Muhammad bin Qasim was sent by Hajjaj under Caliph al-Walid I.

q.s: Which of the following places was NOT taken by Muhammad bin Qasim?
q.x: Somnath was sacked by Mahmud of Ghazni in 1025.

q.s: Which of the following statements about the Arab conquest of Sindh is correct?
o: It was followed by the mass conversion of the people of Sindh.
It was led by Mahmud of Ghazni.
Through it Indian decimal and place-value mathematics reached the Islamic world.
It ended Arab trade with India.
q.x: Indian numerals and astronomy passed to the Arabs and then Europe. There was no mass conversion; non-Muslims paid jizya as protected subjects.

q.s: Who wrote the Shahnama at the court of Mahmud of Ghazni?
q.x: Firdausi, 'Homer of the East', wrote the Shahnama; Unsuri was the poet laureate.

q.s: Al-Biruni's Kitab-ul-Hind was translated into English by:
q.x: Edward Sachau translated it as 'Alberuni's India'.

q.s: The Vimal Vasahi temple at Mount Abu, built by Vimal Shah, is dedicated to:
q.x: The Vimal Vasahi (c. 1031) is dedicated to Adinatha; the Luna Vasahi of Vastupala and Tejpal (1230) is the Neminatha temple.

q.s: The present Somnath temple was rebuilt in 1951 on the initiative of:
q.x: Sardar Patel initiated the rebuilding; the 'Old Somnath' temple was built by Ahilyabai Holkar in 1783.

q.s: The Kandariya Mahadeva temple at Khajuraho was built by which Chandela ruler?
q.x: Vidyadhara built the Kandariya Mahadeva; Khajuraho is in Chhatarpur district of Madhya Pradesh.

q.s: Which of the following was NOT a centre of the Chandela kingdom?
q.x: Dhara was the Paramara capital; Khajuraho, Mahoba and Kalanjar were Chandela centres.

q.s: Which of the following is NOT one of the four Agnikula Rajput clans mentioned by Chand Bardai?
q.x: The Agnikula clans are the Pratiharas, Chaulukyas (Solankis), Paramaras and Chahamanas (Chauhans).

q.s: The Bhojshala at Dhar was originally a temple of which deity?
q.x: The Bhojshala, linked to Raja Bhoja, was a Saraswati (Vagdevi) temple; Muslims call it the Kamal Maula Mosque.

q.s: The Paramara king Bhoja moved his capital from Ujjain to:
q.x: Bhoja shifted the Paramara capital to Dhara (Dhar). The last Paramara, Mahalakadeva, fell to Alauddin Khalji's forces in 1305.

q.s: The Vijaya Stambha at Chittor commemorates Rana Kumbha's victory over:
q.x: Rana Kumbha raised the Vijaya Stambha after defeating Mahmud Khalji of Malwa; he also built Kumbhalgarh.

q.s: The musical treatise 'Sangeet Raj' was written by:
q.x: Rana Kumbha of Mewar wrote the Sangeet Raj.

q.s: In the context of early medieval Rajput society, 'jauhar' refers to:
o: A widow burning on her husband's pyre
Mass self-immolation of women to avoid capture
q.x: Jauhar was mass self-immolation of women when a fort was about to fall; a widow on the pyre is sati, and forced labour was vishti.

q.s: Which of the following statements about early medieval Rajput society is correct?
o: Land grants carried no judicial or police rights.
Sati and jauhar meant the same practice.
Padmini's jauhar at Chittor was against Mahmud Khalji of Malwa.
q.x: Vishti was forced labour; land grants carried judicial and police rights, and Padmini's jauhar was against Alauddin Khalji.

q.s: The Kitab-i-Nauras, a work on music in Dakhni, was written by which Bijapur ruler?
q.x: Ibrahim Adil Shah II wrote it, founded Nauraspur, and Firishta dedicated his history to him.

q.s: The Gol Gumbaz at Bijapur, famous for its whispering gallery, is the tomb of:
q.x: Gol Gumbaz is Muhammad Adil Shah's tomb; the Ibrahim Rauza is Ibrahim Adil Shah II's.

q.s: In the Battle of Raichur (1520), Krishnadevaraya defeated which Bijapur Sultan?
q.x: Krishnadevaraya defeated Ismail Adil Shah and took the Raichur fort.

q.s: Chand Bibi, who defended Ahmadnagar against the Mughals, was the daughter of:
q.x: Chand Bibi was the daughter of Hussain Nizam Shah I and the wife of Ali Adil Shah I of Bijapur.

q.s: Salar Jung I, who introduced the Zillabandi system in Hyderabad, became Diwan in the year:
q.x: Mir Turab Ali Khan became Diwan in 1853 and served three Nizams, abolishing revenue farming.

q.s: Which of the following statements about Salar Jung I is correct?
o: He introduced the Zillabandi system in Hyderabad.
He extended the system of revenue farming.
He was Diwan under Mir Osman Ali Khan.
q.x: Salar Jung I introduced Zillabandi, abolished revenue farming and served three Nizams up to Mahbub Ali Khan.

q.s: Which of the following journals was NOT started by B.R. Ambedkar?
q.x: Young India was Gandhi's; Ambedkar started Mooknayak (1920), Bahishkrit Bharat (1927) and Janata.

q.s: The Independent Labour Party was founded by B.R. Ambedkar in the year:
q.x: Ambedkar founded the ILP in 1936 and the Scheduled Castes Federation in 1942; the RPI was formed in 1957, after his death.

q.s: Which of the following organisations was NOT founded by Ambedkar in his lifetime?
q.x: The RPI was formed in 1957, after his death; the Sabha (1924), ILP (1936) and SCF (1942) were his.

q.s: Who chaired the Minorities Sub-Committee of the Constituent Assembly, of which Ambedkar was a member?
q.x: H.C. Mukherjee chaired the Minorities Sub-Committee; J.B. Kripalani chaired the Fundamental Rights Sub-Committee, both under Patel's Advisory Committee.

q.s: Who was the Constitutional Adviser to the Constituent Assembly, credited by Ambedkar for the rough draft?
q.x: B.N. Rau prepared the rough draft; S.N. Mukherjee was the Chief Draftsman.

q.s: B.R. Ambedkar embraced Buddhism in October 1956 at:
q.x: He converted at Deekshabhoomi, Nagpur on 14 October 1956; the Bharat Ratna came posthumously in 1990.

q.s: B.R. Ambedkar was awarded the Bharat Ratna (posthumously) in the year:
q.x: It was conferred posthumously in 1990.

q.s: On which date did B.R. Ambedkar move the Draft Constitution for consideration in the Constituent Assembly?
q.x: He moved it on 4 November 1948. The Objectives Resolution was Nehru's, moved 13 December 1946 and adopted 22 January 1947.

q.s: Which of the following statements about the Objectives Resolution is correct?
o: It was moved by B.R. Ambedkar.
It was moved by Rajendra Prasad.
q.x: Nehru moved it on 13 December 1946 and it was adopted on 22 January 1947; Ambedkar spoke on it.
